<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
The curve $\Gamma$ specified in Sections~\ref{sec:curve} and~\ref{sec:parameters}
has $w(\Gamma)=1$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:result}
\begin{split}
3.905124162243593023905759435469
 &< L(\Gamma)\\
 &<3.905124162243593023905759435470.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
It is a strict local minimum of $L/w$ within the three-parameter joining
family defined below. Consequently
$m_{\rm open}<3.905124162243594$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:length}
On this joining branch the length is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:length}
 L=2\left(\left\lVert\bar Y-\bar A\right\rVert+\lambda+(2\alpha+u)q_H\right)
       +2\sqrt{b^2+(\beta+p)^2}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Development preserves the lengths of the incoming segment and cone
geodesic. From the joining equations and the signs
$\bar A_y>0$, $\bar Y_y<0$, $\bar T_y<0$
(checked in \path{OpenCurve/RootGraph/DevelopedJoins.lean}) we get
\[
 \bar X-\bar A=-\frac{\bar A_y}{\bar T_y}\bar\mathbf T,
 \qquad
 \bar Y-\bar X=\frac{\bar Y_y}{\bar T_y}\bar\mathbf T,
 \qquad \left\lVert\bar\mathbf T\right\rVert=1.
\]
Both multiples are positive, so $\bar X$ lies between $\bar A$ and
$\bar Y$, so their two lengths sum to $\left\lVert\bar Y-\bar A\right\rVert$.
For the remaining pieces of the arm, we recall from~\eqref{eq:endpoints}
$E-Y=\lambda\mathbf T_-$, from~\eqref{eq:joinB} $B-G=uH'(\alpha)$ and
\[
 H'(\theta)=-h\mathbf e_H+\tfrac12\sin\theta\,\mathbf v_H
                   +\tfrac12\cos\theta\,\mathbf e_z,
 \qquad \left\lVertH'(\theta)\right\rVert=\sqrt{h^2+\tfrac14}=q_H.
\]
The respective lengths are therefore $\lambda$, $2\alpha q_H$ and
$uq_H$. Thus
\[
 L(\mathcal A)=\left\lVert\bar Y-\bar A\right\rVert+\lambda+(2\alpha+u)q_H.
\]
The half-turn image $R(\operatorname{rev}\mathcal A)$ has the same length. For the central portion, including its two tangent leads,
$\left\lVertH_c'\right\rVert=\sqrt{1+k_c^2}$ and each tangent lead has length
$p\sqrt{1+k_c^2}$ by~\eqref{eq:central-trig}. Hence
\begin{align*}
 L(\mathcal C)&=(2p+2\beta)\sqrt{1+k_c^2}\\
 &=2(\beta+p)\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{(\beta+p)^2}}\\
 &=2\sqrt{b^2+(\beta+p)^2}.
\end{align*}
Adding $2L(\mathcal A)+L(\mathcal C)$ proves~\eqref{eq:length}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The curve touches this slab four alternating times, as in the argument by Wienholtz cited in~\cite{Ghomi} and its projection onto the plane whose normal is $\mathbf m$ is the shortest for which we found these four alternating touches. The curves length in that projection is roughly $2.476$, significantly longer than the caliper curve's length of roughly $2.278$ that Ghomi uses in his lower bound on the length of a three-dimensional unit width curve in his Lemma 2.2 and Corollary 3.2. Replacing the caliper curve's length with the length of our projection yields the lower bound for our curve length $3.8896$, below its actual length of roughly $3.905$. Investigating these gaps may be of interest for further work towards proving the minimal length of a unit width curve.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:cover}
If one pair $P,Q\in\mathcal K$ satisfies
$\langle \mathbf n_i,P-Q\rangle\ge\left\lVert\mathbf n_i\right\rVert$ for $i=1,2,3$, then
$W(\mathbf n)\ge\left\lVert\mathbf n\right\rVert$ on $\operatorname{pos}(\mathbf n_1,\mathbf n_2,\mathbf n_3)$.
If all three generators lie in an analytic region defined by homogeneous
linear inequalities, their nonnegative span lies in that region.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
For $\mathbf n=\sum_i\lambda_i\mathbf n_i$, $\lambda_i\ge0$,
\[
 W(\mathbf n)\ge\langle \mathbf n,P-Q\rangle
 \ge\sum_i\lambda_i\left\lVert\mathbf n_i\right\rVert
 \ge\left\lVert\mathbf n\right\rVert.
\]
The second assertion follows by linearity of each defining inequality.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj:global-minimum}
The curve $\Gamma$ is a shortest rectifiable curve in $\mathbb R^3$ of unit width, i.e.
every rectifiable curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^3$ with $w(\gamma)=1$ satisfies
\[
 L(\gamma)\ge L(\Gamma).
\]
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
